title: Truce of Adrianople
text: The Truce of Adrianople in 1547, named after the Ottoman city of Adrianople, was signed between Ferdinand I of Austria and Suleiman the Magnificent. Through this treaty, Ferdinand I of Austria recognized Ottoman control of Hungary, and agreed to pay to the Ottomans a yearly tribute of 30,000 gold florins for his possessions in northern and western Hungary. The Treaty followed important Ottoman victories in Hungary, such as the siege of Esztergom (1543).
